intent: The popup of a MenubarMenu, portalled and placed below its MenubarTrigger in the bar, that lists the menu's items.
typical_uses: The list of actions a MenubarTrigger opens

dont_use_when.situation: A floating panel holding fields, buttons or free-form content
The popup of a nested submenu
The popup of a single menu opened by a trigger outside any bar
The list of options of a form select

invariants.text: Unless `side`, `align`, `sideOffset` or `alignOffset` say otherwise, the popup opens below its trigger, aligned to the trigger's start edge, 8 pixels below it and shifted 4 pixels back along the alignment axis; these placement defaults are the only difference from DropdownMenuContent.
The popup is in the DOM only while the menu is open or animating closed; the kit passes no `keepMounted` to the portal, so a closed menu renders nothing.

Without `container`, the popup portals into the node of the nearest enclosing portal, or the document body when there is none; a theme scoped to a subtree reaches the popup only when that subtree, or a node inside it, is passed as `container`.

dropdown-menu.module.css sets the popup's width to the trigger's width (`--anchor-width`) with a 9rem floor, and caps its height at the space available beside the trigger, scrolling vertically past it.

Arrow keys move focus through the items in order, disabled items included, and wrap from the last back to the first unless the MenubarMenu's `loopFocus` is false; typing moves focus to the next item whose text starts with the typed characters. In a horizontal bar, ArrowRight and ArrowLeft on a row that opens no submenu leave the popup for the neighbouring menu of the bar and open it; on a MenubarSubTrigger the arrow toward the submenu opens that submenu instead.
The popup fades and scales on open and close; under `prefers-reduced-motion` dropdown-menu.module.css drops the transform transition and keeps the fade.

anti_patterns.dont: Keep the default positioning when the trigger sits inside a transformed or filtered container, such as an animated panel
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `positionMethod="fixed"`; absolute positioning resolves against the transformed container instead of the page and misplaces the popup

a11y.by: the primitive's Menu.Popup renders role="menu" and roving focus; menubar.test.tsx asserts the popup is found by the menu role after a trigger click, and that ArrowRight pressed in it closes this menu's items and shows the next menu's

children.states: children is the popup's rows, the parts listed under accepts
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the popup portals into; null and undefined both mean no container of its own
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers. The kit resolves it as `container ?? <the enclosing content's container>`, so an explicit null falls through like an absent prop.

sideOffset.states: sideOffset is the gap in pixels between the anchor and the popup, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
sideOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

alignOffset.states: alignOffset is the shift in pixels along the alignment axis, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
alignOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

collisionBoundary.states: collisionBoundary is the area the popup is kept inside, `clipping-ancestors`, an element, a list of elements or a rectangle
collisionBoundary.because: `'clipping-ancestors' | Element | Element[] | Rect` mixes a string with live DOM elements, which no JSON Schema type covers.

collisionPadding.states: collisionPadding is the space in pixels kept from the collision boundary, one number or a per-side object
collisionPadding.because: `number | { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

finalFocus.states: finalFocus decides where focus goes when the popup closes - true for the default, false for nowhere, a ref, or a function of the interaction type
finalFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` mixes a boolean with a ref object and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the popup's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the popup's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, side, align, nested, instant, transitionStatus). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through dropdown-menu.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside MenubarContent through DropdownMenuContent; only its `container` is exposed, as a prop of the content itself.
Composed inside MenubarContent through DropdownMenuContent; its placement and collision props are exposed on the content itself.

good.title: A File menu in the bar
A popup inside a transformed panel, portalled into a themed subtree

bad.title: Open state passed to the popup
bad.why: The popup takes no open state; `open` and `onOpenChange` belong to the MenubarMenu root.
